scope: Primary-paper context for conditional density and confinement estimates; accessed 2026-11-27. No magnetic-field measurement of KELT-9 or KELT-9b is adopted.

sources.citation: Trammell, Arras & Li (2011), Hot Jupiter Magnetospheres
sources.support: Their isothermal MHD models contain dense closed-field regions alongside escaping streams. Some gas can remain confined beyond the unmagnetized critical equipotential; tidal geometry and field stresses matter. Appendix B supplies the approximate H-proton momentum-transfer frequency used here.
sources.limit: Models and Lyman-alpha applications concern other hot-Jupiter parameters. They do not predict KELT-9b's field, n=2 population, H-alpha source function or present dayside emission. Beta below unity alone is not a stability proof.

sources.citation: Owen & Adams (2014), Magnetically controlled mass loss from extrasolar planets in close orbits
sources.support: Radiation-MHD calculations connect open-field area and mass loss to planetary field, external field and heating. Closed regions suppress part of the outflow; some geometries do not admit a steady transonic flow.
sources.limit: Published field thresholds are not imported as KELT-9b thresholds. The current state has different density, mass loss and radiation, and neither its stellar-field boundary nor stellar-wind pressure has been supplied.

sources.citation: Murray-Clay, Chiang & Murray (2009), Atmospheric Escape from Hot Jupiters
sources.support: The coupled heating/cooling and ionization model includes tides and external pressure; stellar-wind confinement can suppress dayside transonic escape. Radiative losses and recombination affect the mass-flow response to irradiation.
sources.limit: This establishes a mechanism, not the external pressure or slower-flow solution for this KELT-9b atmosphere. A reduced speed cannot simply be inserted while preserving the old momentum and energy balances.

sources.citation: McCann et al. (2019), Morphology of Hydrodynamic Winds
sources.support: Three-dimensional radiation hydrodynamics produces different extended structures as orbital forces and external-wind confinement change. Intermediate confinement can cause nonsteady disruptions, and stronger confinement redirects gas into a tail.
sources.limit: These Lyman-alpha-oriented hydrogen calculations do not establish opaque, cool clumps or their covering fraction in KELT-9b at phase 0.38. Clumping factors below are algebraic controls, not extracted simulation predictions.

sources.citation: Mitani, Nakatani & Yoshida (2022), Stellar Wind Effect on the Atmospheric Escape of Hot Jupiters and their Ly-alpha and H-alpha transits
sources.support: Their dynamically coupled stellar-wind calculations alter the extended outflow but give a comparatively weak H-alpha response because the outermost gas contributes little to that line.
sources.limit: Useful counterexample: more confinement need not yield more H-alpha absorption. It is not a simulation of the presently proposed excited outer reservoir or of the dayside emission data.

sources.citation: Lowson et al. (2023), Multi-epoch detections of the extended atmosphere and transmission spectra of KELT-9b
sources.locations: Abstract and interpretation of the H-alpha transit shape
sources.support: A geometric tail describes their nonstandard transit light curve, but requires excited neutral hydrogen far from the planet and admits stellar center-to-limb alternatives.
sources.limit: This is transit geometry and an ambiguous interpretation, not evidence that a tail covers the present dayside emitter or maintains low n3/n2 at the target phases.

excluded_shortcuts: Do not use unsourced web claims of a detected host-star magnetic field as a boundary condition.
Do not equate a reported volume-equivalent Roche radius with the modeled directional Hill/L1 distance.
Do not carry numerical thresholds from Sun-like hosts or ground-state Lyman-alpha absorption directly to the excited H-alpha layer.
